newsitem.title: USA: Senetek says impotence drug tests well.
newsitem.headline: Senetek says impotence drug tests well.

text.p: Senetek Plc said Tuesday its new drug therapy for treating erectile dysfunction in males -- Invicorp -- was 24 percent more effective in a recent clinical study than prostaglandin El, currently the only drug therapy available in the marketplace for treating male patients with impotence.

The response to test doses in a hospital clinic demonstrated an 80 percent "grade 3 or 4" response to Invicorp in 93 patients, compared to a 56 percent grade 3 or 4 response to 0.01 milligram of prostaglandin El in 70 patients, Senetek said. A "grade 3 or 4" response provides an erection suitable for sexual intercourse.
The study, conducted at Good Hope Hospital, Sutton Coldfield, England, followed 269 patients treated between January 1994 and December 1996.

Phase III clinical trials of Invicorp will conclude soon at 16 sites throughout the United Kingdom, Senetek said, adding that it expects to submit product licensing applications shortly after for approval to market the drug in selective European countries. Pan-European approval then will be sought through a centralized European procedure early next year, Senetek said.
